classification.difficultyReason: Compare rational graphs with horizontal lines, distinguish intersections from poles, and retain the appropriate strict or inclusive endpoints.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=f(x)=\dfrac{6}{x-2}$ and $y=g(x)=3$. The vertical asymptote is $x=2$.

Find their intersection:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{6}{x-2}&=3\\6&=3(x-2)\\x&=4\end{align*}$$
The rational graph is on or above $y=3$ when $2<x\le 4$. The value $x=2$ is undefined.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=f(x)=\dfrac{4}{x+1}$ and $y=g(x)=2$. The vertical asymptote is $x=-1$.

Find their intersection:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{4}{x+1}&=2\\4&=2(x+1)\\x&=1\end{align*}$$
The rational graph is below $y=2$ when $x<-1$ or $x>1$. Exclude the pole $x=-1$ and the equality point $x=1$.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=f(x)=\dfrac{3x+1}{x-2}=3+\dfrac{7}{x-2}$ and $y=g(x)=4$. The asymptotes of $f$ are $x=2$ and $y=3$.

Find their intersection:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{3x+1}{x-2}&=4\\3x+1&=4(x-2)\\x&=9\end{align*}$$
The rational graph is on or below $y=4$ when $x<2$ or $x\ge 9$. The pole $x=2$ is excluded.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{x-3}=2+\dfrac{7}{x-3}$ and $y=g(x)=1$. The asymptotes of $f$ are $x=3$ and $y=2$.

Find their intersection:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2x+1}{x-3}&=1\\2x+1&=x-3\\x&=-4\end{align*}$$
The rational graph is on or below $y=1$ when $-4\le x<3$. Include the intersection $x=-4$ and exclude the pole $x=3$.
